skill.name: markdown-pro
skill.description: Creates professional Markdown documentation, including README files, changelogs, contribution guides, tables of contents, and formatted technical references.
skill.summary: Create structured, consistent Markdown documentation with reusable templates and local helper tools.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline code, example URLs, and placeholder API keys. The helper safely reads git history, but its output option can overwrite any writable path.

remediation.issue: The changelog output option accepts any writable file path and opens it in truncating write mode.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict output to Markdown files within the working directory, reject existing files by default, and require an explicit force option for replacement.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent project documentation makes installation, use, and contribution difficult. This skill supplies structured templates, formatting guidance, and local tools for maintainable Markdown.
actual_capabilities: Creates structured README drafts with installation, usage, API, contribution, and license sections.
Formats changelogs using Keep a Changelog sections and conventional commit categories.
Generates Markdown tables of contents from heading levels through the included Python helper.
Builds changelogs from local git history and can write them to a selected file.
Checks local Markdown links and reports missing targets without requesting external URLs.
Provides templates for README files, changelogs, and contribution guidelines.
limitations: Does not fetch or validate external web links.
Generated content requires project-specific facts, links, commands, and badges.
Changelog generation requires Git and a local repository with readable history.
The helper may overwrite the path supplied to its changelog output option.

use_cases.title: Prepare an open source README
use_cases.description: Turn project facts into a clear README with installation, usage, contribution, and license sections.

use_cases.title: Publish consistent release notes
use_cases.description: Organize local commit history into a categorized changelog that follows common release conventions.

use_cases.title: Standardize technical references
use_cases.description: Format parameters, return values, errors, examples, links, tables, and headings across documentation.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a README
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README for [project]. Include purpose, installation, basic usage, contribution, and license sections. Use only the facts I provide.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new project document from supplied facts.

prompt_templates.title: Create a changelog entry
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Keep a Changelog entry for version [version] from these changes: [changes]. Group items and highlight breaking changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare release notes from a curated change list.

prompt_templates.title: Document an API
prompt_templates.prompt: Format documentation for [API or library] using this interface information: [details]. Include parameters, returns, errors, and one practical example.
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert interface details into a readable technical reference.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a documentation set
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [paths] for structure, heading hierarchy, local links, repeated content, and release consistency. Propose focused edits and explain each change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve several related Markdown files while preserving project facts.

output_examples.input: Create a README for a Python command-line tool that converts CSV files into reports.
output: A concise project overview and feature list.
Installation, command usage, configuration, contribution, and license sections.
Placeholders for verified package names, links, and screenshots.

output_examples.input: Prepare release notes for version 2.1.0 from five features, two fixes, and one breaking change.
output: A dated version section with Added, Fixed, and Breaking Changes groups.
Short entries that preserve issue references and important migration details.

output_examples.input: Review the local documentation links under the docs directory.
output_examples.output: A list of missing local targets with their source documents, while external web links remain unchecked.

best_practices: Provide verified project facts and identify any values that should remain placeholders.
Review generated commands, links, badges, and version numbers before publishing.
Use the helper on a version-controlled working tree and inspect changes before replacement.
anti_patterns: Do not publish placeholder credentials, repository names, domains, or package commands.
Do not generate release notes from unreviewed commit messages without checking accuracy and relevance.
Do not write changelog output over an existing file without preserving its current content.

faq.question: Can this skill create a complete README?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure and format a README when you provide accurate project details.

faq.question: Does it generate changelogs from Git?
faq.answer: Yes. The helper reads local git history and groups conventional commit messages into changelog sections.

faq.question: Does link validation contact external websites?
faq.answer: No. The helper skips HTTP, HTTPS, email, and anchor links, then checks local targets only.

faq.question: Can it update an existing document?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the document and state which facts, sections, or formatting must remain unchanged.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: Basic guidance requires no extra software. Helper commands require Python, and changelog generation also requires Git.

faq.question: Will the helper overwrite files?
faq.answer: The changelog command writes to the supplied output path and can replace existing content. Review the path before execution.
